Evan B.: Hi @people-ops — noticed Maryland state tax and a ‘Local Tax — Baltimore City’ line on my 11/15 paystub but I live in Philadelphia and we have a PA/MD reciprocity. I shouldn’t have MD withheld. Can someone check?
Sophia (People Ops): Sorry to see that, @Evan. Can you paste the paystub snippet or last4 so payroll can pull the run?
Evan B.: Last4 3321. Paystub snippet: 
```
Payrun: 2024-11-15
EmpID: 3321
Work location: Remote (PA)
State tax withheld: Maryland $210.00
Local tax withheld: Baltimore City $45.00
Net pay: $1,730.00
```
Payroll Bot: Ticket created: PAY-6142 assigned to @Nora (Payroll). Initial review ETA 1 business day.
Nora (Payroll): Pulled the file. Payroll jurisdiction = MD-BALT because the office location on the employee record is still set to MD-BAL-OFFICE. HR change to PA home address was entered on 2024-08-01 but the office flag didn’t flip. Looks like cross-system mapping issue between HR and Facilities.
Nora (Payroll): Quick plan: 1) reverse the MD & local city withholdings in a reversal batch if remittance not yet sent 2) process an off-cycle credit for the amounts if remitted 3) update employee jurisdiction and audit other remote PA employees who show MD withholding.
Tax Team: Note on reciprocity: PA/MD reciprocity requires employee to file form MW507 (Maryland) to be exempt; employer must withhold PA only once employee has the exemption on file. If employee provided MW507 earlier, we need to confirm it was attached prior to the payroll cut. If not, employee can file MW507 and request refund, but employer-side correction is preferable. Also Baltimore local tax should not apply to non-residents unless work location flagged in MD.
Facilities: We did update desk assignments in July when Evan went fully remote, but we didn’t have a required step to clear the ‘primary-office’ field for offboarded desks. Well backfill the primary-office attribute for remote reassignments from July onward.
Manager - Priya: Evan, do you have a copy of MW507 or anything you submitted?
Evan B.: I submitted MW507 on 2024-08-05 via onboarding portal. I can forward confirmation email.
Nora (Payroll): Please forward that to payroll@ so I can attach. If MW507 was present before file creation we can submit an adjustment and avoid employee reclaim. If not present, payroll credit + tax reclaim workflow will be needed.
Sophia (People Ops): Actions: 
 @Nora submit reversal/off-cycle plan (PAY-6142)
 @Tax Team advise on whether MW507 presence allows retroactive reversal vs payroll credit
 @Facilities backfill primary-office flags for remote reassignments since 2024-07-01
 @Evan please forward MW507 confirmation to payroll@ so we can attach to the record
Nora (Payroll): ETA: Ill confirm remittance window for MD liabilities today. If remittance not sent well reverse in this payroll period. If remitted, Ill schedule off-cycle credit within 5 business days and Tax will open refund request with Comptroller.
Tax Team: If we need to request refund from MD Comptroller, expect 30-90 days processing. For employee experience we recommend payroll credit immediately and then pursue the state reclaim.
Evan B.: Thanks that works. Please CC me on PAY-6142 and any docs I need to sign or resubmit.
Nora (Payroll): Will do. Posting PAY-6142 in the ticket now and will update this thread once reversal/credit is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
